newsitem.title: UK: UK OFWAT UNHAPPY WITH WATER FIRMS' DIV INFORMATION.
newsitem.headline: UK OFWAT UNHAPPY WITH WATER FIRMS' DIV INFORMATION.

text.p: British water industry regulator Ofwat said on Friday it was disappointed with water companies' explanations over its dividend levels and depreciation charges.
Director general Ian Byatt said that the companies' annual returns contain "disappointly scant information" in these two key areas.

"Most companies have paid scant attention to financial matters in their overviews and detail was lacking in two particularly important areas -- the basis of the utility's dividend and the relationship between depreciation and expenditure on capital maintenance for non-infrastructure assets," Byatt said in a statement.
He has asked all the companies to provide "commentary" on these issues by September 5.
Byatt has criticised companies in the past for inadequate explanations for the basis of dividends paid by the utility company to its parent group.
Ofwat will seek a change in the licences so that companies have to disclose the utility dividend publicly if they remain unwilling to provide the necessary explanations.

Ofwat was also concerned that depreciation charges may be allocated to profit and loss accounts at above the levels of expenditure necessary to maintain surface assets -- treatment works and buildings.
"I expect that actual capital maintenance expenditure should, in the medium term, be broadly equivalent to the current cost depreciation charge," said Byatt.
The latest returns show that capital investment increased significantly in 1996/97 compared with 1995/96.
All the companies are required by their licence to make an annual return each July to the director general covering their activities in the previous year.
